01 / The question

Do changing privacy interfaces make the choices promised in policy accessible?

Why this matters

Privacy is experienced through both policy language and interface actions. ConsentDiff connects these two layers over time, rather than treating a policy document or a consent banner as an isolated snapshot.

02 / Contribution & method

My contribution

As sole author, I connected policy changes with observable consent-interface behavior through a longitudinal audit.

Role & scope

As sole author, I developed the longitudinal audit approach connecting policy changes with observable consent-interface behavior. The work brings together semantic clause alignment, interface classification, and a weighted claim–UI alignment measure.

01Observe over time＋

Observe over time

Snapshot sites monthly and align policy clauses semantically to track clause-level changes.

02Inspect the interface＋

Inspect the interface

Combine DOM signals and screenshot cues to classify consent-UI patterns.

03Connect claims to actions＋

Connect claims to actions

Map policy claims to observable predicates and compare alignment across time, regions, and verticals.

04 / The next question

How can longitudinal audits distinguish a clearer interface from a change that truly improves user agency?

A direction to explore

Observable interface alignment provides one form of evidence. Understanding whether people can recognize and exercise their choices also calls for user-centered evaluation. This is a proposed extension of the audit.
